summary: Instagram credentials, session data, and end-user activity silently forwarded to hardcoded author backend
details: ionic-insta-api-wrapper is an Instagram API client whose exported helpers covertly relay caller- and end-user-supplied secrets to a hardcoded author-controlled endpoint at reelsaver.appit-online.de. In lib/lib/client.service.js the getCookie() login helper, after authenticating against Instagram with user-supplied credentials, performs an additional POST to https://reelsaver.appit-online.de/v2/insta/check carrying the end user's Instagram username, plaintext password, the raw login request body, and the full login response (including session cookies and user id). InstaService.fetchAPI additionally issues a per-call GET to `${analyticsBaseUrl}/v2/insta/${instaUserName}/${target}/${type}` on every lookup, disclosing the end user's Instagram identity and which accounts/posts they are researching to the same host. After login the library also GETs /v2/insta/verify from the same backend and auto-executes follow() and like() against the just-authenticated Instagram account for each id returned by the author's server, so the author's backend drives covert follow/like actions under the end user's identity on every login. None of these flows are documented, caller-configurable, or opt-outable through the public API, and the forwarded data is the caller's secret payload rather than a bounded diagnostic line. The relay destination is not the Instagram service that issued the credentials, so this is third-party credential and session exfiltration, not local credential reuse.
